conviction_note: Two insurance lead-gen peers (EverQuote, MediaAlpha) reported after TREE last spoke. Each beat a Q3 guide set the same week TREE set its own, and each guided Q4 strongly. Insurance is about two thirds of TREE's revenue, so its Q3 insurance line and Q4 insurance budget probably clear a guide-midpoint consensus. Against that, TREE fell 19.6% last print even though insurance grew 42% and peers beat, because SMB and the guide drove the move. The stock is also up 13.6% over 20 days and 3.6% today, so part of the peer read is likely already in the price. p_up is held at 56 on a large move scale of 18 (median of the last 8 prints is 20.9, no usable option chain), giving +2.16. The findings sum to +4.4 because each peer document is sized on its own; that gap is the reaction-function caveat, not an inconsistency.
bar: Company Q3 2026 guide (Q2 8-K, 2026-07-29): revenue $325-335m, VMM $88-93m, adj EBITDA $34-36m; FY2026 revenue $1.30-1.32bn, VMM $364-374m, adj EBITDA $145-152m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001434621/000162828026050633/tree-63026xer.htm). The revenue consensus sits at the guide midpoint: $330.3m per Earnings Whispers 2026-10-26 (https://finviz.com/news/408409/lendingtrees-smb-slump-faces-a-key-test-as-shares-sit-near-post-earnings-lows), and $329.7-329.8m per other trackers. Two sources agree on revenue. Adj EPS is less settled: $1.29 (EW, whisper $1.26) against $1.18-1.26 elsewhere. Q3 2025 comparison: revenue $307.8m, insurance $203.5m, consumer $66.2m, home $38.1m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1434621/000162828025047318/tree-93025xer.htm), so the guide implies revenue growth slowing from +25% to about +7%.
positioning_check: Short interest 1,052,405 shares on the 2026-10-15 settlement (7.5% of 14.04m shares outstanding, 7.8% of float). It was 1,108,646 on 09-30 and 846,359 on 08-14, so it rose about 24% since August. Days to cover rose from 1.48 to 4.25 (https://equibles.com/stocks/tree/shortinterest; stockanalysis.com shows 7.81% of float and a 3.27-day ratio, updated 2026-11-03). That is elevated but not crowded. Skew is unavailable: the baseline rejected a 40-vol-point 25d skew as implausible and the ATM spread is 86% of mid, so the option market gives no usable directional statement. The put/call open-interest ratio is 0.78. The tape shows the stock 58.7% below its 52-week high, +13.6% over 20 days, +7.1% over 5 days and +3.6% intraday today. It is up from a $23.50 post-Q2 low, and the CEO's tax withholding on 2026-09-30 was struck at $24.35.

findings.finding: Insurance lead-gen peers that report after TREE beat Q3 guides set the same week as TREE's own (late July). EverQuote's Q3 revenue was $218.1m (+25% YoY) against a $198-208m guide (+7% vs the midpoint), with auto +21% and home/renters +70%. MediaAlpha's revenue was $375.9m (+23%) against a $330-355m guide (+10% vs the midpoint). Insurance was 67% of TREE's Q2 revenue ($209.3m, +42%). If TREE's insurance grew sequentially like EverQuote's auto line (+10.6% Q/Q), insurance would be about $231m, and total revenue would land above the top of TREE's $325-335m guide, against a $330.3m consensus sitting at the midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Insurance strength has not saved this stock. In Q2 2026 insurance revenue grew 42% and MediaAlpha beat consensus the same evening, yet TREE fell 19.6% on SMB weakness, a big adj EPS miss ($0.68 vs $1.41) and a lowered FY outlook. TREE's Q2 revenue of $313.4m missed the $315.6m consensus even though peers beat. The last 8 prints moved a median 20.9% in absolute terms.
findings.why_not_priced: EverQuote reported last night, less than one session before TREE. TREE's consensus was not revised: it still sits at the $330m guide midpoint and drifted down from about $337m (EW 2026-10-26). If the street had priced the peer beats, revenue estimates would sit above the guide top. Part of the read may already be in today's +3.6% and the 20-day +13.6% run-up, which is why this is sized below the name's median move.
findings.independence: MediaAlpha's Q3 8-K (2026-10-28, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000263/maxq32026-earningsreleasex.htm) points the same way: revenue $375.9m against a $330-355m guide, contribution $57.4m against $51.5-54.5m. Progressive's Q3 10-Q shows advertising up about 18% YoY to about $1.6bn, homeowners new applications +22% and personal-lines new applications slightly down (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000379/pgr-20260930.htm). These are peer and counterparty documents, not TREE's own number. Finding 2 rests on the same EverQuote and MediaAlpha releases, but on their Q4 lines.

findings.finding: The same peers' forward statements show carrier budgets still expanding into Q4. EverQuote guided Q4 revenue to $213-223m (midpoint about $218m) against a pre-report consensus of $211.9m, saying carriers 'continue to maintain strong underwriting profitability and an appetite for growth'. MediaAlpha guided Q4 revenue to $355-375m (+25% YoY at the midpoint) and said carriers are 'committing meaningful budgets in both home and auto insurance'. TREE's implied Q4 guide comes from FY2026 revenue of $1.30-1.32bn and VMM of $364-374m, which the street read as a cut in July. The peers' Q4 lines argue the insurance part of that implied Q4 is not at risk of a further cut and has room to be firmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock traded on. In July a Q3 revenue guide 2% below consensus and a lowered FY outlook (EBITDA midpoint $148.5m vs $157.9m consensus) produced -19.6%. The April 2026 print was -21.7% and March was +23.9%. Moves of about 20% in either direction follow the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: TREE's Q4 consensus (about $339.5m revenue per one tracker) was set off July's guide cut and has not been revised since the peers spoke. If it had, Q4 estimates would have moved up after October 28 and November 2, and nothing shows that. SMB and consumer, not insurance, are the parts of TREE's guide the street doubts, so this lands on half of the guide question only.
findings.independence: Shares documents with finding 1 (the EverQuote 8-K of 2026-11-02 at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001640428/000119312526443633/ever-ex99_1.htm and the MediaAlpha 8-K), read on their Q4 lines rather than their Q3 lines. Progressive's 10-Q shows ad spend still growing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000379/pgr-20260930.htm). This is a proxy, not TREE's own guide.

findings.finding: SMB lender appetite stayed strong through Q3. Enova's small-business originations were about $1.8bn (+28% YoY, up from $1.6bn in Q2), and its SMB receivables were +34% YoY at 9/30. TREE's SMB weakness was the stated cause of the July drop. Its revised guide assumes lenders recover and merchants do not, and the CFO said lender appetite on the network 'has since stabilized'. Enova's growth supports the lender side of that assumption, not the merchant-demand side.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line drove the last print: weak SMB demand plus higher costs produced -19.6% on 2026-07-29. Consumer segment revenue was $60.3m in Q2 (-4% YoY), against $66.2m in Q3 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-26) frames SMB as the open question and says the market 'has leaned toward a longer slowdown'. A market pricing SMB recovery would not have the stock sitting near its post-earnings low. This is a proxy for one input, the lender side. The $1.8bn segment figure comes from a transcript summary; the primary release confirms only the +34% receivables growth.
findings.independence: TREE's own Q2 8-K says lender appetite stabilised after the quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001434621/000162828026050633/tree-63026xer.htm). Earnings Whispers reports management calling July the best sales month since Q1. This is a lender-side proxy only; nothing found measures merchant demand.

findings.finding: Peer unit economics held or improved in Q3, which argues against TREE's insurance VMM squeeze getting worse. TREE's VMM fell to 28% of revenue in Q2 from 33%, blamed on Google traffic costs and carrier competition. EverQuote's variable marketing dollars were $62.6m on $218.1m revenue (28.7%), against a guide-implied 28.3%. MediaAlpha's contribution margin rose to 15.3% from 14.9% YoY, with contribution of $57.4m above its $51.5-54.5m guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July, VMM up only 4% on revenue up 25%, together with a lower FY VMM range ($364-374m vs a prior $378-395m), was part of the -19.6% move.
findings.why_not_priced: The preview names VMM margin as 'the more telling signal' and treats the squeeze as ongoing. If peers' stable margins were priced, TREE would not still trade near its lows with the VMM guide unrevised. This is an inference across companies: TREE's squeeze may be company-specific (its traffic mix), so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Shares the EverQuote document with findings 1-2. MediaAlpha's contribution margin comes from a separate 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000263/maxq32026-earningsreleasex.htm). There is nothing TREE-specific.

findings.finding: Shorts built into the print. Short interest rose from 846k shares (08-14) to 1.05-1.11m (09-30/10-15), and days to cover rose from 1.48 to 4.25, while the stock rallied about 19% off its $23.50 low to $28.07. Shorts at 7.8% of float and 4 days of volume add squeeze fuel if the guide holds. They are not crowded enough to act as a mechanism on their own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior squeeze episode on record for TREE prints. The +22.5% to +23.9% up-moves (2025-03, 2025-07, 2026-03) show the stock can gap 20% or more on a good guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, not a fact outside it. It enters as asymmetry: a 4.25 days-to-cover short base on a $394m cap amplifies a positive surprise more than a negative one. The sign is genuinely two-way, because rising shorts can also be informed selling, so the size is small.
findings.independence: stockanalysis.com statistics (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/TREE/statistics/, updated 2026-11-03) show 1.05m short, 7.81% of float and a 3.27-day ratio.

findings.finding: There is balance-sheet room for a capital-return announcement. Net leverage fell to 1.9x and free cash flow is about $80m a year (EW preview), against a market cap of about $394m. H1 2026 operating cash flow was $40.7m, cash was $110.8m at 6/30 (up from $81.1m), and no buybacks were made in H1 2026. An authorization at the print is possible, but nothing announces one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback announcement in the last 8 prints, so there is no history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference from a sourced balance sheet, not a sourced intention. An implied 20% FCF yield on a stock 59% off its high suggests the market is not crediting capital return. If the market expected a buyback, the preview and the analysts would be discussing one.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-26 (https://finviz.com/news/408409/lendingtrees-smb-slump-faces-a-key-test-as-shares-sit-near-post-earnings-lows) mentions leverage of 1.9x opening the door to buybacks. It is a secondary read of the same balance sheet.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew to agree or disagree with. The positive lean agrees with the 20-day +13.6% run-up and today's +3.6%, so part of the peer read is likely priced. The name's last two prints (-21.7%, -19.6%) were sold on the guide despite strong insurance, so p_up stays close to 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): TREE fell 19.6% in July with insurance +42% and peers beating, so finding 1 (peer Q3 beats, insurance revenue) went from +2.0 to +1.5, and p_up from 57 to 56.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): finding 4 (peer margins as a VMM proxy) went from +0.5 to +0.4, and finding 6 (buyback capacity, an inference) from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest of 7.8% of float with 4.25 days to cover is not crowded; finding 5 went from +0.5 to +0.3 because the sign is two-way.

Lesson 'two readings of one document': findings 1, 2 and 4 share the EverQuote and MediaAlpha releases. They are kept apart because they land on different lines (Q3 revenue, Q4 guide, VMM margin), and the shared source is stated in independence. Progressive was merged into finding 1 rather than filed separately.
Lesson 6 (bar): the revenue bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing trackers. EPS is disputed ($1.18-1.29), so no finding sizes on EPS.
Left standing: finding 2 (Q4 guide line) at +1.5, because guidance is the line this stock trades on and a peer print after the company last spoke is the 'what has worked' pattern.
